w: A festive day that is remembered as the Diksha-day of Lord Swaminarayan, day of appointment of Lord Swaminarayan as Head of the Satsang Fellowship by Ramanand Swami and the day on which HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj was initiated into Parshad diksha. Also, according to the Puranas it is celebrated as Prabodhini Ekadashi (or Dev Uthi Ekadashi) and Tulsi vivah.

After the morning arti, while Swamishri was circumambulating the mandir, a few novices (sadhaks) and sadhus were each holding a piece of paper. Each paper had different sized zeros drawn on it. As Swamishri came by, he humorously referred to each shape of zeros held by a corresponding sadhak: "I am long, I am fat, I am round, I am uneven." The novices said, "Swami Bapa! We are zeros of different shapes and sizes but you are the numeral 1. Through your association we (the zeros) have attained worth. Swamishri responded: "Yes, that is true, God and His holy sadhu is 1. Through the association of Yogiji Maharaj you have… (attained worth)." Swamishri then blessed the novices and sadhus.

Several active and enthusiastic youths of Sarangpur were introduced to Swamishri. Whenever the need arises, these youths selflessly offer voluntary services in Sarangpur and the neighboring villages. Swamishri was pleased by their spirit of service and advised, "Sarangpur is a pilgrim place. And there should be purity and piety here. Don't allow gambling, liquor and meat-eating in the village. Since you are offering your noble services in the village, do bear this in mind."
At 7.05 pm, a Parents Day program commenced. The youths performed a drama on Lalabhai's (of Upleta) faith.
At 10.30 a.m. Swamishri arrived in Dausa and sanctified a plot of land for a hari mandir. Swamishri addressed the devotees, blessed them and departed for Manpur.
At 11.00 a.m. Swamishri arrived at Manpur and observed the sculpting of stones for the Akshardham project. After blessing the craftsmen Swamishri departed for Sikandra.

After traveling 11-12 km Swamishri arrived at Sikandra workshop at 11.45 a.m. After performing pujan and arti of a mandir, Swamishri observed the workmanship of craftsmen sculpting stones for the Akshardham project. As Swamishri weaved his way through the workshop he blessed the craftsmen.
Swamishri arrived back in Jaipur at 8.00 p.m.
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of six BAPS hari mandirs; Sirpur and Sahada (Khandesh region), Khanjroli, Madharkui, Kamalapor and Sathvav.

At 8:30, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat to offer his meal to Thakorji. Meanwhile two sadhus from Valsad gave their reports. Akhandmangal Swami, who had come from Valsad, said, "About 300 boys and girls have come here today on a pilgrimage. We were actually supposed to leave, but when the kishores learnt that you were here, they all insisted, 'We want to stay here tonight and leave only after having darshan tomorrow.' So today we have sent them all to Mahelav for darshan, and they will come back tonight. We have arranged their accommodation around the village here. Bhandari Swami (the sadhu in charge of the kitchen) has work here, so they will all join in the seva."

On hearing this, Swamishri said, "The kishores have travelled for two days to come here, so they must be tired. So tell Bhandari Swami there is no need to make the kishores work now. As soon as they arrive, let them all go to sleep. They have to leave again tomorrow."

After giving them this instruction, even when all the sadhus had gone out after the meal, he said to his attendant sadhu, "Go and tell the Bhandari not to put these boys and girls to any other seva. We should keep in mind that they have all come tired out, and that tomorrow they have to get up early and leave again."
Even at the age of 90, Swamishri constantly worries that the pilgrim kishores should not have any trouble. This is Swamishri's true heartfelt affection for the kishores.

The festival of Kartiki Purnima and Guru Purnima has always been celebrated in Bochasan since the time of Shastriji Maharaj. Pramukh Swami Maharaj too celebrates that festival here. As satsang has spread, the places for these festivals keep becoming too small. That is why this time, so that the arrangements could be managed, it had been planned to celebrate the festival in the Bhareliya field owned by the mandir. Kothari Vedagna Swami told Swamishri about the arrangements for this festival.
Finally a sadhu said, "Yogiji Maharaj did dhun, but you showed courage and acquired a great deal of land."
Swamishri said, "Everything goes on through his dhun alone; nothing is done by us. Mandirs have increased, satsang has increased; all this happens through his dhun alone."

At 8.30 Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat to feed Thakorji. Meanwhile two sadhus from Valsad gave their reports. Akhandmangal Swami, who had come from Valsad, said, "About 300 teenage boys and girls have come here today on a pilgrimage. Really, we were supposed to leave, but when the teenagers learnt that you were here, they all insisted, 'We want to stay here tonight and leave only after darshan tomorrow.' So today we have sent everyone to Mahelav for darshan, and after that they will come back at night. Lodging has been arranged around the village here. Bhandari Swami (the storekeeper) has work here, so they will all join in the seva."

As soon as he heard this, Swamishri said, "The teenagers have come after travelling for two days, so they must be tired. So tell Bhandari Swami there is no need to make the teenagers work now. As soon as they come, put them all to bed. Tomorrow they have to set off again."

After giving him this instruction, after the meal, even when all the sadhus had gone out, he said to the attendant sadhu, "Go and tell the storekeeper not to put these teenage boys and girls to any other seva. He should consider that they have all come tired out, and tomorrow they have to get up early and leave again."
Even at the age of 90, Swamishri constantly worries that the pilgrim teenagers should have no trouble. This is the true affection of Swamishri's heart for teenagers.

Today before the shangar arti, Mahant Swami Maharaj came onto the podium of the mandir. Here a youth studying at the Vidyanagar hostel had brought Pramukh Swami Maharaj's face wonderfully to life with an artistic rangoli. Seeing it, Swamishri was very pleased. At that time the hostel youths prayed to him, "You will take us to Akshardham in this very body, won't you?"
"Yes, that is our very business," Swamishri said, pleased, clapping his hands.
Hearing this, all the youths too broke into applause.

Today in the central shrine, Thakorji had been dressed in pitambar (yellow silk garments). Diamond studded ornaments had been placed on his chest. So the darshan was beautiful. But Swamishri's vision comes steeped in devotion. So Mahant Swami Maharaj at once told the pujari sadhu, "It is winter now. So do not keep such garments. Thakorji will feel cold. Now dress him in closed garments (trousers, pyjamas and so on)."

Having said this, he performed the shangar arti. After that, again having darshan in all three shrines, as he was leaving from near Shastriji Maharaj's shrine, he told the pujari sadhu, "Make the tassel of Shastriji Maharaj's mala shorter. (A long one) is awkward when turning it."
Such subtle thoughts are possible only when there is constant oneness with God and the guru.

Today, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was leaving, Abhayswarupdas Swami brought Shrirang Lange, joint secretary of Urban Development of Maharashtra, to meet him. The meeting lasted only a few moments in the lift, but he was so impressed that tears welled up in his eyes. Then, describing his experience, he said, "The divinity and the purity that were in the eyes of Pramukh Swami Maharaj are in the eyes of Mahant Swami Maharaj too."
Everyone has such clear and firm experiences. The reason is that this is the same Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

ds.p: On the flight from Mumbai to Anand
w: As soon as the plane took off into the Mumbai sky, knowing Mahant Swami Maharaj's wish, Hariprakashdas Swami began to have Harikrishna Maharaj look upon the land of Mumbai through the plane's window. After a while Swamishri said, "The sun is coming in there."
After some time water was given to Swamishri to drink, but Swamishri turned his face a little to one side and drank it.
Gurumanandas Swami asked, "Why like this, Swami?"
Swamishri pointed to Thakorji installed in front.
What subtle decorum! One should not even drink water in front of Thakorji.
